newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia Interior Minister quits in presidential bid.
newsitem.headline: Colombia Interior Minister quits in presidential bid.

text.p: Colombia's Interior Minister Horacio Serpa has submitted a letter of resignation to President Ernesto Samper to prepare a bid for the presidency, government sources confirmed on Tuesday.
The Radionet radio network reported Samper had accepted the resignation of his right-hand man around midday (1700 GMT) but there was no official confirmation of that.
Serpa, a member of the ruling Liberal Party, has been at the helm of the Interior Ministry since Samper took office in August 1994.

He has earned himself a reputation as the president's staunchest ally within the cabinet, leading political analysts to suggest that if Serpa were elected president he would pursue similar policies to those of the Samper administration.

Serpa has been in the front-lines defending Samper against accusations that he financed his 1994 election campaign with money from the powerful Cali drug cartel. He has also been outspoken in his attacks against the United States and its ambassador to Bogota, Myles Frechette, whom he recently called a "sick gringo" for what he claimed was the envoy's constant meddling in internal Colombian affairs.
